title: Elements are built in stars, and some sites are still open

body: The 1957 review "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars," by E. Margaret Burbidge, G. R. Burbidge, William A. Fowler, and Fred Hoyle, is the classic account of how nuclear reactions in stars build chemical elements. It is a synthesis of nuclear physics and astronomy, not a claim that every nucleus is made in the same kind of star. Which astrophysical sites dominate the heaviest nuclei has been revised since 1957. In 2017 LIGO and Virgo reported GW170817, gravitational waves from a binary neutron-star inspiral. A companion paper reported optical emission from a kilonova following that merger. A kilonova is one observed channel relevant to heavy-element production. What fraction of the heaviest elements comes from mergers, and what fraction from other sites, is not settled by those two papers.
